simple.meaning: סָפַק (çâphaq) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to clap the hands (in token of compact, derision, grief, indignation, or punishment); by implication of satisfaction, to be enough ; by implication of excess, to vomit.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 10 times across Numbers, 1 Kings, Job, Isaiah, Jeremiah, and 2 more, beginning at Numbers 24:10. Its meaning is built by comparing the passages where Scripture uses it.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to סָפַק (H5606).

definitions.short: to clap the hands (in token of compact, derision, grief, indignation, or punishment); by implication of satisfaction, to be enough ; by implication of excess, to vomit
definitions.full: H5606. saphaq II. [ שָׂפַק ] verb suffice (Late Hebrew סָפַק suffice, abound , so Ecclus 15:18 +; סְפַק סְפֵיק, ᵑ7 , Syriac ; Arabic is be niggardly, scanty , Lane 1573 ); — Qal Imperfect 3masculine singular יִשְׂמֹּק 1Kin 20:10 , subject dust, with לְ of thing.
definitions.rootNote: or שָׂפַק ; (1 Kings 20:10; Job 27:23; Isaiah 2:6), a primitive root;

occurrences.englishText: Balak’s anger burned against Balaam, and he struck his hands together. Balak said to Balaam, “I called you to curse my enemies, and, behold, you have altogether blessed them these three times.
Ben Hadad sent to him, and said, “The gods do so to me, and more also, if the dust of Samaria will be enough for handfuls for all the people who follow me.”
Men will clap their hands at him,
He strikes them as wicked men
For he adds rebellion to his sin.
For you have forsaken your people, the house of Jacob,
Surely after that I was turned.
All that pass by clap their hands at you.
I will also strike my hands together,
